input.quote: Company acknowledges that Contractor provides consulting and development services to other clients, and agrees that nothing in this Agreement shall be deemed or construed to prevent Contractor from delivering on such business.
input.rationale: Full-document review (purpose/engagement scope § 1, ownership/IP § 4, warranties § 5, termination § 6, and all miscellaneous provisions §§ 7–19) shows no covenant restricting the businesses Clear Capital may operate or the products it may buy, build, or market. The only competition-adjacent language in § 4(b) runs the other way: Company acknowledges Contractor's freedom to serve other clients, which is a restriction-free acknowledgment binding us only to tolerate Contractor's other business. § 4(b)(ii) limits our resale or other use of Contractor's own pre-existing proprietary materials to the software we receive, but that is ordinary licence-scope wording for Vendor IP, not a field-of-use or non-compete restriction on our own products or business, and § 4(c) separately licenses Contractor's Information for our business operations. § 13 is a mutual personnel non-solicitation, which is a distinct commercial term and is not flagged here as a non-compete. The Agreement therefore meets the preferred position — no non-compete or field-of-use restriction on Customer — so no redline is proposed.

mappings.element: Customer has no non-compete or field-of-use restriction.
